messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache size anomaly on prod-cluster-7. Metric kv_cache_items spiked from ~120k -> 1.2M in ~6m. Error rate for streaming endpoints (spec-decode path) increased. Pager triggered (P1). Link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-0421

morgan (on-call): taking first responder. joining now. any known deploys?

eng-runtime: not that we know. autoscaler did a restart on 7a ~5m ago but no model rollouts. we saw continuous-batching queue depth jump.

morgan (on-call): ok. putting mitigation plan in place: 1) disable speculative decoding on runtime for prod-cluster-7 2) reduce max_batch_size for continuous-batcher 3) monitor tail latencies and costs.

raj: +1. I can flip speculative decoding flag. will do it in 2m, will also open a short-lived patch param. tagging @taylor for batch config change.

morgan (on-call): doing a quick customer impact check — CS, any customers calling in?

customer-success: we have 3 alerts from enterprise customers noticing higher token usage and a few complaints about timeouts on long multi-turn prompts. not yet SLA pages but escalating.

support-ops: seeing spike in user-facing 502s for streaming endpoints in us-east-1. correlates with requests that hit >6 draft tokens before target flush.

morgan (on-call): ok go for hotfixs. raj, paste command you run so we have audit entry.

raj: running immediate toggle: 
```
# disable speculative decoding for prod-cluster-7
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/clusters/prod-cluster-7/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRLPLANE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"speculative_decoding": {"enabled": false, "reason": "kv-cache blowup mitigation"}}'
```
Executing now.

incident-bot: ACTION: Config change submitted by raj at 2026-04-21T14:08:11Z.

raj: response: 200 OK. speculative_decoding.enabled=false applied.

morgan (on-call): taylor, can you push batch cap change? reduce max_batch_size from 128 -> 32 and set per-queue ttl to 150ms. We want to avoid giant batches that blow the KV cache.

taylor: will do. applying hotpatch to continuous-batcher config via infra API.

taylor: patch command:
```
PATCH /infra/continuous-batcher/prod-cluster-7
{"max_batch_size": 32, "enqueue_ttl_ms": 150}
```
applied in canary across 2 nodes first.

incident-bot: Canary rollout started at 2026-04-21T14:12:40Z (nodes: node-7a,node-7b).

support-ops: after toggle + canary batch change: kv_cache_items on those nodes dropped from 1.1M -> 130k within ~90s. user-traffic error rate down ~65%.

morgan (on-call): great. rolling to rest of cluster now if no regressions.

eng-runtime: note — speculative decoding could produce redundant KV writes when draft/target sync diverges; combo with large batches can exponentially multiply cache entries. We're tracking hypothesis: speculative decoding duplicate caches + unbounded batching -> blowup.

sre-lead: good call to disable. please save current heap profiles and KV cache dumps for postmortem. runbook link: runbooks/kv_cache_blowup.md (follow sections 2-4).

raj: grabbing heap/profile snapshots now:
```
# quick dumps
ssh node-7c sudo /opt/bin/dump-kv-cache --out /tmp/kvdump-7c.json.gz
kubectl exec -n infra node-7c -- /usr/local/bin/heapdump > /tmp/heap-7c.hprof
```
uploaded to s3://incidents/1749001234/artifacts/

taylor: I'm seeing a small latency bump in canary for short prompt requests (~15ms). acceptable tradeoff to stop blowups.

customer-success: update to customers: we've applied emergency mitigations (disabled speculative decoding + batch caps) — we expect error rates to fall within 10m. CS will message affected accounts.

morgan (on-call): handing active incident to raj (on-call secondary) — I'm stepping off for a brief handover. current state: mitigations applied cluster-wide at 14:18Z, metrics trending down. stay on until stabilization.

raj: ack. taking over. @sre-lead can you own postmortem coordination? I'll keep monitoring for 60m.

sre-lead: yes, I'm on postmortem. initial blameless timeline will be created. Please capture: exact sequence of config changes, canary metrics, heap dumps, and the model/endpoint IDs with highest cache churn.

eng-runtime: additional note for investigation: we suspect a subtle interaction where speculative decoding drafts are keyed separately from target caches; when draft tokens are produced out-of-order or repeated due to resends, the KV cache key space balloons. We'll add stronger dedupe and TTL bounding in the runtime.

raj: a few quick numbers (post-mitigation):
- total kv_cache_items peak: 1.25M
- peak memory attributed to kv cache: ~18.6GB
- 10-min token cost spike for top affected customer: 8.9x
- downstream 502s dropped 72% after mitigations

support-ops: monitors will run with tighter alert thresholds for 24h. creating synthetic load to validate stability.

morgan (on-call): passing final notes: schedule 1h review with eng-runtime + SRE + CS to confirm root cause and next steps (dedupe, TTL, batching heuristics). keep incident flagged P1 until we have a postmortem draft.

customer-success: customers informed. one enterprise wants a timeline for mitigation steps — CS will draft and share.

sre-lead: assigned follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: improve dedupe & add TTL cap (owner: @eng-runtime)
- infra: add defensive hard cap on batch size at infra layer (owner: taylor)
- product: evaluate spec-decoding rollout gating and add canary metrics (owner: product)
Please tag owners in the doc.

morgan (on-call): closing active pager for now. leave thread open for updates and postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity de-escalated to P2 at 2026-04-21T15:09:30Z. Artifacts: s3://incidents/1749001234/. Postmortem assigned to sre-lead.

raj: I'll keep monitoring dashboards for 60m and then hand back to next rotation. thanks all for quick responses.

morgan (on-call): thanks team. good job moving fast and keeping customers informed.
